data.title: Modernize CI, add code coverage, and replace broken type generator

epic.spec:
# Modernize CI, Add Code Coverage, and Replace Broken Type Generator

## Overview

Three workstreams:
1. **CI modernization**: Update runner images (macos-26), bump stale action versions, delete legacy `build/` directory, update README
2. **Code coverage**: Add coverage collection and reporting to CI following the Humanizer pattern
3. **Type generator replacement**: Replace the broken PowerShell/TypedocConverter pipeline with a proper ts-morph parser + .NET CLI emitter, with tests

**Why the generator must be replaced:** The current `GenerateMonacoTypings/` pipeline uses TypeDoc 0.20.37 + TypeScript 4.2.4 + TypedocConverter (unmaintained since 2023). Monaco 0.54.0 uses TypeScript 5.x features that break TypeDoc parsing. The pipeline is silently broken — nothing tests whether it can parse current `monaco.d.ts`. This was only caught by manual inspection, not by automated tests. The `SerializationContractTests.cs` tests the output types but not the generator pipeline itself.

**Architecture for new generator:**
```
monaco.d.ts
    │  (ts-morph, Node.js)
    ▼
intermediate-model.json   ← clean schema we control
    │  (.NET CLI tool)
    ▼
*.cs files                ← STJ-attributed, matching existing patterns
```

**Why hybrid?** TypeScript parsing MUST happen in Node.js (canonical, always-current compiler). C# emission benefits from being a .NET tool (debuggable, testable with Verify snapshots, integrates with existing .NET build).

## Scope

**In scope:**
- Update `macos-15` → `macos-26` runner in ci.yml
- Update stale action versions in `tag-release/action.yml` and `nuget-uno-publish/action.yml`
- Delete entire `build/` directory (4 legacy files)
- Fix stale "UWP" signing label
- Update README.md (remove VS 2019, UWP framing, Legacy Edge)
- Add code coverage (Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.CodeCoverage + ReportGenerator)
- Build ts-morph type extractor (Node.js → intermediate JSON)
- Build .NET CLI tool for C# emission (reads JSON → emits .cs files)
- Add generator pipeline tests (snapshot + round-trip + compilation)
- Delete old `GenerateMonacoTypings/` PowerShell scripts after migration

**Out of scope:**
- `wasm-tools-net9` workload removal (owned by fn-3.3)
- `copilot-setup-steps.yml` changes
- `install-dependencies.ps1` (confirmed active — local dev setup script)

## Task dependency graph

```
.1 (CI runners)  .2 (build/ + README)  .4 (ts-morph parser)
       │                                        │
       ▼                                        ▼
.3 (coverage)                            .5 (.NET CLI emitter)
                                                │
                                                ▼
                                   .6 (tests + migration)
```

- Tasks .1, .2, .4 are independent (parallelizable)
- Task .3 depends on .1 (both edit ci.yml)
- Task .5 depends on .4 (needs intermediate JSON schema)
- Task .6 depends on .4 + .5 (needs both tools to test and migrate)

## Quick commands

```bash
# Build solution
dotnet build MonacoEditorComponent.slnx --no-restore

# Run tests with coverage
dotnet test MonacoEditorComponent.Tests --coverage --results-directory ./TestResults

# Run the new type extractor (after task .4)
node tools/monaco-type-extractor/src/index.ts node_modules/monaco-editor/monaco.d.ts -o tools/monaco-type-extractor/output/model.json

# Run the new .NET emitter (after task .5)
dotnet run --project tools/MonacoTypeEmitter -- --input tools/monaco-type-extractor/output/model.json --output MonacoEditorComponent/Monaco/
```

## Acceptance

**CI modernization (Tasks .1, .2):**
- [ ] `build-macos` job uses `runs-on: macos-26` (Task .1)
- [ ] `tag-release/action.yml` uses `actions/checkout@v4`, `setup-dotnet@v4`, .NET 10.0.x, NBGV 3.8.118 (Task .1)
- [ ] `nuget-uno-publish/action.yml` uses .NET 10.0.x (Task .1)
- [ ] Signing description says "Uno Monaco Editor" (no "UWP") (Task .1)
- [ ] `build/` directory deleted, no dangling refs in `.github/**`, `README.md`, `AGENTS.md` (Task .2)
- [ ] README.md modernized: .NET 10, browserwasm + desktop targets, no VS 2019/Legacy Edge (Task .2)

**Code coverage (Task .3):**
- [ ] `MonacoEditorComponent.Tests.csproj` references `Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.CodeCoverage` (Task .3)
- [ ] Coverage version pinned in `Directory.Packages.props` (Task .3)
- [ ] CI produces coverage artifact (HTML + Cobertura XML) at deterministic path (Task .3)

**Type generator (Tasks .4, .5, .6):**
- [ ] ts-morph extractor parses current `monaco.d.ts` (TS 5.x) and produces intermediate JSON (Task .4)
- [ ] Intermediate JSON schema captures: interfaces, enums (string + numeric), type aliases, properties (name, type, optional), inheritance, namespaces (Task .4)
- [ ] .NET CLI tool reads intermediate JSON and emits C# files matching existing patterns: STJ attributes, `JsonStringEnumConverter<T>`, `JsonStringEnumMemberName`, `InterfaceToClassConverter`, nullable properties (Task .5)
- [ ] .NET CLI tool respects `.generator-ignore` (15 hand-tuned files never overwritten) (Task .5)
- [ ] Generator pipeline has snapshot tests (known .d.ts input → verified .cs output) (Task .6)
- [ ] Generator pipeline has a smoke test: parse current `monaco.d.ts` → emit C# → `dotnet build` succeeds (Task .6)
- [ ] Old `GenerateMonacoTypings/` PowerShell scripts deleted (Task .6)
- [ ] AGENTS.md and README.md updated to reference new tool (Task .6)

## References

- [ts-morph](https://github.com/dsherret/ts-morph) (5.9k stars) — TS AST parser, supports TS 5.x natively
- [TypedocConverter](https://github.com/hez2010/TypedocConverter) — current (broken) tool, last updated 2023
- [Humanizer CI/coverage](https://github.com/Humanizr/Humanizer) — coverage reference implementation
- [Verify](https://github.com/VerifyTests/Verify) (3.4k stars) — snapshot testing for .NET
- [macOS 26 beta — actions/runner-images#13008](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/13008)
- Existing patterns: `MonacoEditorComponent/Monaco/Editor/*.cs`, `SerializationContractTests.cs`

## Risks

- **macOS 26 is beta**: Rollback rule: revert to `macos-15` if runner-image failures for 3+ consecutive runs.
- **Intermediate JSON schema design**: Must capture enough TS type information for faithful C# emission. Iterative refinement expected — snapshot tests catch regressions.
- **Generator output drift**: New generator may produce slightly different C# than hand-tuned files. The `.generator-ignore` mechanism protects hand-tuned files; snapshot tests lock down generated output.
- **Test coverage gap was silent**: The broken pipeline was only caught by manual inspection. The new pipeline tests prevent this class of regression.

Update CI runner images and GitHub Action versions to latest in the targeted composite actions and main CI workflow.

# fn-4-update-ci-runner-images-delete-stale.3 Add code coverage collection and reporting to CI

## Description
Add code coverage collection and reporting to the CI pipeline, following the Humanizer project pattern (`Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.CodeCoverage` + ReportGenerator).

**Size:** M
**Files:** `MonacoEditorComponent.Tests/MonacoEditorComponent.Tests.csproj`, `Directory.Packages.props`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (desktop-tests job only — after Task .1 completes)

**Depends on:** Task .1 (both edit `ci.yml`)

## Approach

Follow the [Humanizer](https://github.com/Humanizr/Humanizer) reference implementation:

1. **Add coverage package via central package management:**
   - Add version entry in `Directory.Packages.props`: `<PackageVersion Include="Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.CodeCoverage" Version="18.0.4" />`
   - Add package reference in `MonacoEditorComponent.Tests/MonacoEditorComponent.Tests.csproj`: `<PackageReference Include="Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.CodeCoverage" PrivateAssets="all" />`

2. **Update CI `desktop-tests` job** in `ci.yml`:
   - Add `--coverage` flag to `dotnet test` command
   - Add `--results-directory $(Agent.TempDirectory)/TestResults` (or GitHub Actions equivalent like `${{ runner.temp }}/TestResults`) for deterministic output path
   - Coverage collects on DesktopCDP test subset only (the tests this job runs)

3. **Add ReportGenerator step** after tests in `desktop-tests` job:
   - Use `danielpalme/ReportGenerator-GitHub-Action` to generate HTML + Cobertura reports
   - Input: `${{ runner.temp }}/TestResults/**/*.cobertura.xml`
   - Output: `${{ runner.temp }}/CoverageReport/`
   - Report types: `HtmlInline;Cobertura;Badges`

4. **Upload coverage artifact:**
   - Use `actions/upload-artifact` to upload the coverage report directory
   - Artifact name: `coverage-report`

5. **Add coverage configuration** (optional `testconfig.json` or inline):
   - Format: Cobertura
   - Exclude generated code: `GeneratedCodeAttribute`, `ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute`, `DebuggerHiddenAttribute`, `DebuggerNonUserCodeAttribute`

## Key context

- Humanizer uses `Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.CodeCoverage` v18.0.4 (Microsoft's first-party tool), NOT coverlet.
- This project uses central package management (`ManagePackageVersionsCentrally=true` in `Directory.Build.props`). All package versions must go in `Directory.Packages.props`.
- Coverage is collected on the DesktopCDP test subset only — this should be clearly labeled, not presented as full project coverage.
- Humanizer does NOT enforce coverage thresholds — coverage is informational only. Follow this approach.
## Approach

Follow the [Humanizer](https://github.com/Humanizr/Humanizer) reference implementation:

1. **Add coverage collector to test project(s):**
   - Add `Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.CodeCoverage` package reference to test project(s)
   - Ensure test project uses Microsoft Testing Platform runner (`UseMicrosoftTestingPlatformRunner`)

2. **Update CI test step** in `desktop-tests` job:
   - Add `--coverage` flag to `dotnet test` command
   - This produces Cobertura XML output automatically

3. **Add coverage report generation step** after tests:
   - Use `danielpalme/ReportGenerator-GitHub-Action` to generate HTML + Cobertura reports from coverage XML
   - Upload coverage report as a build artifact via `actions/upload-artifact`

4. **Optional: Add coverage configuration** (`testconfig.json` or inline):
   - Format: Cobertura
   - Exclude generated code attributes: `GeneratedCodeAttribute`, `ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute`, `DebuggerHiddenAttribute`, `DebuggerNonUserCodeAttribute`

## Key context

- Humanizer uses `Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.CodeCoverage` v18.0.4, NOT coverlet — this is Microsoft's first-party coverage tool for the new Testing Platform.
- Humanizer uses ReportGenerator v5 to produce `HtmlInline`, `Cobertura`, and `Badges` report types.
- Humanizer does NOT enforce coverage thresholds — coverage is informational only.
- The `desktop-tests` job (ci.yml L119) runs on `windows-latest` and executes `dotnet test` — this is the natural place to add coverage.
- The WASM `build` job doesn't run tests, so no coverage there.
- Coverage instrumentation adds ~10-20% overhead to test execution time.
## Acceptance
- [ ] `Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.CodeCoverage` version pinned in `Directory.Packages.props`
- [ ] `MonacoEditorComponent.Tests.csproj` references `Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.CodeCoverage` with `PrivateAssets="all"`
- [ ] `desktop-tests` CI job passes `--coverage` and `--results-directory` flags to `dotnet test`
- [ ] CI produces Cobertura XML coverage data at a deterministic path
- [ ] CI generates HTML coverage report via `danielpalme/ReportGenerator-GitHub-Action`
- [ ] Coverage report uploaded as `coverage-report` build artifact
- [ ] Generated/excluded code filtered from coverage (GeneratedCode, ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attributes)
- [ ] Coverage collection does not break existing test execution

data.title: Create ts-morph Monaco type extractor (Node.js parser)

tasks.spec:
# fn-4-modernize-ci-add-code-coverage-and.4 Create ts-morph Monaco type extractor (Node.js parser)

## Description
Create a Node.js tool using ts-morph that parses `monaco.d.ts` and produces a clean intermediate JSON model. This replaces the broken TypeDoc 0.20.37 + TypedocConverter pipeline that cannot handle TypeScript 5.x.

**Size:** M
**Files:** `tools/monaco-type-extractor/` (new directory): `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `src/index.ts`, `src/extractor.ts`, `src/model.ts` (JSON schema types)

## Approach

- Use ts-morph (v27+) which bundles its own TS compiler and handles TS 5.x natively
- Parse `monaco.d.ts` via `project.addSourceFileAtPath()` 
- Walk top-level declarations: `getInterfaces()`, `getEnums()`, `getTypeAliases()`
- Handle Monaco-specific patterns:
  - Nested namespaces (`monaco.editor`, `monaco.languages`)
  - String-backed enums (TS string literal unions → enum with string values)
  - Numeric enums (preserve integer values)
  - Optional properties (`hasQuestionToken()` → nullable in C#)
  - Interface inheritance (`getExtends()`)
  - Generic type parameters
- Output: `intermediate-model.json` with a well-defined schema
- The JSON schema is the contract between this tool and the .NET emitter (Task .5)

## Key context

- ts-morph v27 bundles its own TypeScript compiler — no version conflicts with the project's root TS version
- Monaco's `monaco.d.ts` uses nested `declare namespace monaco { ... }` blocks — extractor must walk into module declarations
- Current pipeline extracts ~100+ interfaces and ~30+ enums from Monaco's API surface
- The intermediate model must distinguish string-backed enums (need `JsonStringEnumConverter`) from numeric enums (no converter) — this is a critical distinction for the .NET emitter
- Reference real-world ts-morph parsers: `elastic/elasticsearch-specification`, `lynx-family/lynx`, `RoryDuncan/ts2cs`
## Acceptance
- [ ] `tools/monaco-type-extractor/` directory exists with `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, and TypeScript source
- [ ] ts-morph is the sole parsing dependency (no TypeDoc, no TypedocConverter)
- [ ] Extractor successfully parses current `monaco.d.ts` (TS 5.x) without errors
- [ ] Intermediate JSON contains: interfaces (with properties, methods, inheritance), enums (string + numeric distinguished), type aliases, namespaces
- [ ] Each property in the model includes: name, type text, optional flag, JSDoc comment (if any)
- [ ] Each enum member includes: name, value (string or number), and value kind
- [ ] `node tools/monaco-type-extractor/src/index.ts monaco.d.ts` produces valid JSON output
- [ ] JSON schema is documented (either as TypeScript types in `model.ts` or as JSON Schema)
## Done summary
TBD

data.title: Create .NET CLI tool for C# type emission from intermediate model

tasks.spec:
# fn-4-modernize-ci-add-code-coverage-and.5 Create .NET CLI tool for C# type emission from intermediate model

## Description
Create a .NET CLI tool (console app or dotnet tool) that reads the intermediate JSON model from Task .4 and emits C# files matching the existing patterns in `MonacoEditorComponent/Monaco/`.

**Size:** M
**Files:** `tools/MonacoTypeEmitter/` (new project): `MonacoTypeEmitter.csproj`, `Program.cs`, emitter logic files. Add project to `MonacoEditorComponent.slnx`.

**Depends on:** Task .4 (intermediate JSON schema)

## Approach

- Create a .NET console app (`OutputType=Exe`, `TargetFramework=net10.0`)
- Read intermediate JSON model via `System.Text.Json` deserialization
- Emit C# files matching five existing patterns (from `MonacoEditorComponent/Monaco/`):
  - **String-backed enums**: `[JsonConverter(typeof(JsonStringEnumConverter<T>))]` + `[JsonStringEnumMemberName("value")]` + `[EnumMember(Value = "value")]` per member
  - **Numeric enums**: plain enum with integer values, no converter attributes
  - **Model classes**: `public sealed class` with auto-properties, nullable for optional props
  - **Interface types**: `[JsonConverter(typeof(InterfaceToClassConverter<IFoo, Foo>))]` pattern
  - **Namespace mapping**: `monaco.editor` → `Monaco.Editor`, `monaco.languages` → `Monaco.Languages`
- Respect `.generator-ignore` file: read the ignore list, skip emission for those filenames
- Add `// <auto-generated />` header and `#nullable enable` to all generated files
- Use `CamelCase` property naming convention (matches `MonacoJsonContext` global policy — no explicit `[JsonPropertyName]` needed on most properties)

## Key context

- The `MonacoJsonContext` at `MonacoEditorComponent/Serialization/MonacoJsonContext.cs` uses global CamelCase naming + WhenWritingNull — generated types must conform
- 15 files in `.generator-ignore` are hand-tuned and must never be overwritten (see `GenerateMonacoTypings/.generator-ignore`)
- The tool absorbs logic from `postprocess-stj.ps1` (7 transforms) — no separate post-processor needed
- Could use `PackAsTool` for NuGet distribution, but a simple console app is fine for internal use
- Consider single-file publish for portability if desired
## Acceptance
- [ ] `tools/MonacoTypeEmitter/` project exists and builds with `dotnet build`
- [ ] Project added to `MonacoEditorComponent.slnx`
- [ ] Tool reads intermediate JSON from Task .4 and emits `.cs` files
- [ ] Emitted string-backed enums use `[JsonConverter(typeof(JsonStringEnumConverter<T>))]` + `[JsonStringEnumMemberName]`
- [ ] Emitted numeric enums have no converter attributes, only integer values
- [ ] Emitted model classes are `sealed` with nullable auto-properties for optional fields
- [ ] Emitted interfaces use `[JsonConverter(typeof(InterfaceToClassConverter<IFoo, Foo>))]`
- [ ] All emitted files have `// <auto-generated />` header and `#nullable enable`
- [ ] `.generator-ignore` is respected — 15 hand-tuned files are never overwritten
- [ ] `dotnet run --project tools/MonacoTypeEmitter -- --input model.json --output ./out/` produces valid C# files
## Done summary
TBD

- Commits:
- Tests:
- PRs:

data.title: Add generator pipeline tests and replace old GenerateMonacoTypings scripts

tasks.spec:
# fn-4-modernize-ci-add-code-coverage-and.6 Add generator pipeline tests and replace old GenerateMonacoTypings scripts

## Description
Add comprehensive tests for the new generator pipeline, verify output against existing C# files, then delete the old `GenerateMonacoTypings/` PowerShell scripts and update docs.

**Size:** M
**Files:** `tools/MonacoTypeEmitter.Tests/` (new test project), `GenerateMonacoTypings/` (delete), `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`

**Depends on:** Tasks .4 and .5 (needs both tools to test)

## Approach

**Tests (three levels):**

1. **Snapshot tests** (Verify): Feed known `.d.ts` fragments to the extractor, pipe intermediate JSON through the emitter, compare C# output against `.verified.cs` snapshots. Catches any drift in generated output.

2. **Smoke test (full pipeline)**: Parse real `monaco.d.ts` → intermediate JSON → emit C# → `dotnet build` the emitted files. This is the test that would have caught the TypedocConverter breakage — if parsing fails, the test fails immediately.

3. **Round-trip tests**: For key types (MarkerData, CompletionItem, etc.), verify generated C# types serialize/deserialize identically to the existing hand-verified types. Leverages existing `SerializationContractTests` as the gold standard.

**Migration:**
- Run new generator against current `monaco.d.ts`
- Diff output against existing `MonacoEditorComponent/Monaco/` files (excluding `.generator-ignore` files)
- Resolve any differences (may reveal bugs in old pipeline or improvements in new one)
- Delete `GenerateMonacoTypings/` directory (all scripts, package.json, README.md, .generator-ignore)
- Move `.generator-ignore` to `tools/MonacoTypeEmitter/` (or equivalent config)
- Update AGENTS.md "Key Directories" section and "GenerateMonacoTypings" references
- Update README.md references
- Update `.gitignore` entries (lines 287-288) and `.gitattributes` (line 68)
